item.title: Radical Innovation in the Creative Industries
item.content:encoded:
Roberto Verganti, Stockholm School of Economics

Joris Ebbers, Luiss Business School

Thorsten Hennig-Thurau, University of Münster

Gerda Gemser, University of Melbourne

Paola Bellis, Politecnico di Milano

This special issue addresses the gap in understanding how radical innovations emerge and succeed in creative industries such as music, film, design, and video games. While research has focused on creative production and incremental changes, little is known about radically new creative outcomes that depart from existing conventions and how organizations can create and market these breakthroughs.

The call invites papers examining how radical innovations develop, the underlying creative processes and enabling factors, and strategies for market acceptance. Research across individual, team, firm, and network levels is encouraged, with particular interest in how emerging technologies influence radical innovation and how digital platforms and algorithmic systems reshape audience discovery and legitimization of radical creative works.

Appel publié par Journal of Product Innovation Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Characterization and measurement of radical creative outcomes versus regular creative production
  • Impact of radical innovation on business success and performance determinants
  • Optimal distinctiveness and balancing continuity with novelty in creative outcomes
  • Creative processes and factors enabling radical innovation in creative industries
  • Role of new digital technologies (AI, extended realities) in generating radical creative outcomes
  • Leadership and management approaches supporting radical creative output
  • Organizational practices and routines enabling radically new creative outcomes
  • Evolution of creative outcomes from emerging to established status
  • Key actors and 'misfits' facilitating radical innovation
  • Market preparation and audience education for radical creative outcomes
  • Consumer adoption barriers and strategies to overcome them
  • Communicative approaches and storytelling for radical creative outcomes
  • Word of mouth, advertising, and communication strategies for radical innovations
  • Distribution strategies and role of digital technology in market acceptance
  • Role of gatekeepers (critics, curators) in recognizing and legitimizing radical innovations
  • Impact of algorithmic recommender systems on recognition and diffusion of radical outcomes
  • Influence of digital platforms on genres and market acceptance of radical innovations

item.title: Entrepreneurship as an Artist: Subjectivities, Contexts and Collective Dynamics
item.content:encoded:
Joëlle Bissonnette, Université du Québec à Montréal

Elen Riot, Université Paris 8

Christian Makaya, Ascencia School of Business

Céline Barredy, Université Paris Nanterre

Vanessa Serret, Université de Lorraine

This special issue examines entrepreneurial practices of artists in their activities of creation, production and dissemination. While management has long been characterized as an art due to its creative and non-iterative dimension, the relationship between artistic and managerial spheres has historically been presented as antagonistic or dichotomous. However, contemporary research reveals a growing convergence between the figures of the artist and the entrepreneur, notably through shared practices and approaches.

This convergence also reflects the growing proportion of artists becoming entrepreneurs in a socioeconomic context marked by injunctions to entrepreneurship and innovation, as well as by increasing precarity in artistic creation activities. These approaches highlight initiatives carried out by individuals often marginalized geographically or socio-culturally who mobilize cultural, social and emotional resources to create value within their communities. They also reveal the interrelations, sometimes fruitful and sometimes more harmful, between artistic creation and entrepreneurial practices and the challenges facing artistic entrepreneurs.

Appel publié par Revue internationale P M E Économie et gestion de la petite et moyenne entreprise. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Personal narratives, emotions and individual artistic trajectories and their influence on entrepreneurial practices
  • Context as a creative resource and entrepreneurial catalyst: how artists transform contextual constraints into opportunities
  • Individual-collective dynamics in artistic entrepreneurship: articulation between individual artistic expression and community engagement
  • Artistic entrepreneurship as a response to contemporary challenges: resilience strategies, alternative economic models, and sustainable development
  • Artists' relationship with their personal histories, emotions, identity negotiations and bifurcations, and their influence on entrepreneurial practices
  • How broader contextual dynamics (social, technological, environmental, political) shape and inspire artists' entrepreneurial trajectories
  • Interaction dynamics between individual artistic interests and collective action, particularly regarding tensions between personal creative expression and collaborative community engagement
  • Hybrid organizational models emerging between individual creation and collective action
  • Collaborative practices and their role in generating collective intelligence and artistic innovation
  • Governance mechanisms in artistic collectives for balancing individual expression and shared objectives
  • Role of artistic interventions in community resilience and social transformation
  • Artists' strategies for resisting and adapting to market pressures while maintaining economic viability
  • Balance between creative integrity and institutional or commercial commitments
  • Social and environmental innovations developed by artist-entrepreneurs
  • Contributions of artistic entrepreneurship to sustainable development objectives
